title: Adjunct normal form of the iterated scalar mates
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, and let $X\xrightarrow rY\xrightarrow sZ$ be arbitrary scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme]. Work in the ordinary unbounded small-etale derived categories $D_R(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Q_T=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $P_{u,R}=u_R^*$ for exact constant-ring inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $R_{u,R}=Ru_{*,R}$, with canonical adjunction $P_{u,R}\dashv R_{u,R}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{u,R}$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Use the normalized isomorphism $\lambda_u:P_{u,B}Q_T\cong Q_WP_{u,A}$ for $u:W\to T$ [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], and write $\chi_u:Q_TR_{u,A}\to R_{u,B}Q_W$ for its counit-defined mate [def-pur-etale-scalar-mate]. For $M\in D_A(X)$ put $U=R_{r,A}M$, $V=R_{s,A}U$. For any $h:Q_ZV\to R_{s,B}R_{r,B}Q_XM$, define its composite-adjunction adjunct by
$$\operatorname{Adj}_B(h)=\varepsilon_{r,B,Q_XM}\circ P_{r,B}(\varepsilon_{s,B,R_{r,B}Q_XM})\circ P_{r,B}P_{s,B}(h),$$
using the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].
Put
$$G_M=R_{s,B}(\chi_{r,M})\circ\chi_{s,U}:Q_ZV\longrightarrow R_{s,B}R_{r,B}Q_XM.$$
Then $\operatorname{Adj}_B(G_M)=T_M$, where
$$T_M=Q_X(\varepsilon_{r,A,M})\circ Q_X(P_{r,A}(\varepsilon_{s,A,U}))\circ\lambda_{r,P_{s,A}V}\circ P_{r,B}(\lambda_{s,V}):P_{r,B}P_{s,B}Q_ZV\longrightarrow Q_XM.$$
The equality concerns the specified scalar mates, without assuming either mate invertible or imposing boundedness, properness or coefficient flatness.

source.place: Tag 0E46, label remark-compose-base-change: the adjunct of the successive two square mates; explicit coefficient-change specialization of the omitted verification

proof.text:
For $u=r,s$ and an object $K$ on its source, the definition [def-pur-etale-scalar-mate] and the adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] give
$$\varepsilon_{u,B,Q_WK}\circ P_{u,B}(\chi_{u,K})=Q_W(\varepsilon_{u,A,K})\circ\lambda_{u,R_{u,A}K}.\tag{E}$$
Here $u:W\to T$; use $(u,K)=(r,M)$ and $(s,U)$. This applies to the specified mate, without an isomorphy assumption.

source.place: Tag 0E46, remark-compose-base-change, omitted verification, specialized to coefficient squares; Categories Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following paragraph

proof.text:
Put $N=R_{r,B}Q_XM$ and $a=\chi_{r,M}:Q_YU\to N$. The counit of the given adjunction [def-kun-projection-formula-map] is a natural transformation, so its naturality axiom at $a$ is
$$\varepsilon_{s,B,N}\circ P_{s,B}R_{s,B}(a)=a\circ\varepsilon_{s,B,Q_YU}.$$
Expand $G_M$ and the displayed definition of $\operatorname{Adj}_B$, distribute $P_{r,B}P_{s,B}$ over composition, and substitute this equation:
$$\operatorname{Adj}_B(G_M)=\varepsilon_{r,B,Q_XM}\circ P_{r,B}(a)\circ P_{r,B}(\varepsilon_{s,B,Q_YU}\circ P_{s,B}(\chi_{s,U})).$$

source.place: Tag 0E46, remark-compose-base-change, omitted verification, specialized to coefficient squares; Categories Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following paragraph

proof.text:
Substitute (E) for $(s,U)$ into the final factor of step 2 and for $(r,M)$ into its first two factors. Functoriality and associativity give
$$\operatorname{Adj}_B(G_M)=Q_X(\varepsilon_{r,A,M})\circ\lambda_{r,U}\circ P_{r,B}(Q_Y(\varepsilon_{s,A,U}))\circ P_{r,B}(\lambda_{s,V}).$$
All substitutions are equalities of arrows in $D_B(X)$; no inverse of $\chi_r$ or $\chi_s$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 0E46, remark-compose-base-change, omitted verification, specialized to coefficient squares; Categories Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following paragraph

proof.text:
By [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], $\lambda_r$ is a natural isomorphism. Its naturality axiom at $\varepsilon_{s,A,U}:P_{s,A}V\to U$ reads
$$\lambda_{r,U}\circ P_{r,B}(Q_Y(\varepsilon_{s,A,U}))=Q_X(P_{r,A}(\varepsilon_{s,A,U}))\circ\lambda_{r,P_{s,A}V}.$$
Substituting this into step 3 gives exactly $T_M$. The two naturality equations and (E) hold for every object of the unbounded categories, so no boundedness, properness or coefficient-flatness condition enters.

lean.statement: theorem scalarMate_iterated_adjunct {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B] (φ : A →+* B) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (r : X ⟶ Y) (s : Y ⟶ Z) (M : DerivedCategoryModule A X) : scalarIteratedAdjunct φ r s M ((scalarMate φ s).app (R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r).obj M) ≫ R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) s).map ((scalarMate φ r).app M)) = L(upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) r).map ((scalarPullbackIso φ s).hom.app (R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) s).obj (R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r).obj M))) ≫ (scalarPullbackIso φ r).hom.app (L(upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) s).obj (R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) s).obj (R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r).obj M))) ≫ (scalarExtension φ X).map (L(upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r).map ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) s).counit.app (R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r).obj M))) ≫ (scalarExtension φ X).map ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r).counit.app M)
lean.note: The helper scalarIteratedAdjunct explicitly defines Adj_B(h) for every arrow h with the specified endpoints.
